learningObjectives: Identify major DMN nodes and subsystems.
Explain the DMN beyond the misleading idea of “rest”.
Relate DMN processes to memory, self and social cognition.
Interpret clinical associations without treating them as biomarkers.

anatomy.label: Medial prefrontal cortex
anatomy.detail: Medial prefrontal regions contribute to self-related evaluation, social inference and value integration.
anatomy.clinical: Altered self-appraisal and rumination may recruit these processes.

anatomy.label: Posterior cingulate / precuneus
anatomy.detail: Posterior midline regions participate in autobiographical, contextual and internally directed processing.
anatomy.clinical: They are commonly examined in depression, dementia and disorders of consciousness.

anatomy.label: Angular gyrus
anatomy.detail: Angular regions help integrate multimodal meaning and memory-related information.
anatomy.clinical: Damage can disrupt complex semantic and attentional operations.

anatomy.label: Medial temporal subsystem
anatomy.detail: Hippocampal and parahippocampal interactions support scene construction and episodic simulation.
anatomy.clinical: Trauma and memory disorders can alter the content and accessibility of internal simulation.

anatomy.label: DMN subsystems
anatomy.detail: The DMN contains interacting subsystems rather than one uniform circuit.
anatomy.clinical: Different symptoms may involve different nodes or coupling patterns.

interaction.title: Default Mode Network sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow information flow across the network.

stages.label: Disengage
stages.text: External task demand falls or attention turns inward.

stages.label: Retrieve
stages.text: Autobiographical and semantic information becomes available.

stages.label: Simulate
stages.text: The brain constructs a self-, social- or future-oriented model.

stages.label: Integrate
stages.text: Internal models are compared with goals and current context.

quizBank.question: The DMN is most accurately described as:
options: A distributed system supporting several internally oriented processes
A single structure in the frontal lobe
A network active only during sleep
quizBank.explanation: The DMN supports multiple internally oriented functions.

quizBank.question: A commonly described DMN core node is the:
quizBank.explanation: Posterior cingulate/precuneus is a key DMN hub.

quizBank.question: Task-related DMN suppression means:
options: Relative reduction during some externally demanding tasks
The person has no inner speech
quizBank.explanation: Suppression is relative and task dependent.

quizBank.question: The DMN may support:
quizBank.explanation: Memory-based internal simulation is a central DMN function.

quizBank.question: Clinical DMN findings are best treated as:
options: Proof of rumination in one person
quizBank.explanation: DMN findings are heterogeneous and not diagnostic at the individual level.
